# Bank of Wenzhou Co., Ltd. Notes to Financial Statements of 2007

## 1. General Information

##### (i) History

Wenzhou City Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. (The "bank") is a joint-stock commercial bank founded pursuant to the policy in the Notice of Establishing City Cooperative Banks (GF [1995] No.25) published by the State Council and upon the Approval of the Opening of Wenzhou City Commercial Bank (YF [1998] No.395) issued by the People's Bank of China. The Bank received Business License for Enterprise as Legal Person numbered 3300001005495 issued by Zhejiang Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce on March 10, 1999. The former name of the Bank was Wenzhou City Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., which was renamed Bank of Wenzhou Co., Ltd. in line with the Approval of Change of Name of Wenzhou City Commercial Bank (YJF (2007) No.375) issued and approved by China Banking Regulatory Commission on September 6, 2007. The Bank received Business License for Enterprise as Legal Person issued by Zhejiang Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce on September 25, 2007 after the change of name.

The Bank had a registered capital of RMB 290,495,800 yuan. In February 2004, it increased a registered capital of RMB 180,300,000 yuan and registered capital was changed to 470,795,800 yuan. In June 2006, it increased registered capital for the second time, in which 50,233,900 yuan was transferred from capital reserve and undistributed profit, and 486,183,800 yuan was newly invested by 17 enterprise corporate shareholders and 257 employee shareholders. The registered capital was changed to 1,007,213,500 yuan. In December 2006, it increased a registered capital of RMB 15,968,400 yuan and registered capital was changed to RMB 1,023,181,900 yuan. As of December 31, 2007, the biggest shareholder of the Bank was China Huarong Assets Management Company, holding 8.17% of the shares of the Bank.

As of December 31, 2007, the registration number of the Business License for Enterprise as Legal Person of the Bank was 330000000008227 and the registration number of the License for Financial Business Operation was B0153H233030001. The legal representative of the Bank was Xia Ruizhou and registered address 1# Build –ing, Huahai Plaza, Chezhan Avenue, Wenzhou.

##### (ii) Setup of Business Organizations

As of December 31, 2007, the Bank had a Headquarters and 58 branches. They are the Headquarters, Quzhou Branch, Yueqing Sub-branch, Ruian Sub-branch, Pingyang Sub-branch, Yongjia Sub-branch, Liushi Sub-branch, Tangxia Sub-branch, Hongqiao Sub-branch, Lucheng Sub-branch, Ouhai Sub-branch, Longwan Sub-branch, Guoding Sub-branch, Fuqian Sub-branch, Jinying Sub-branch, Fulong Sub-branch, Desheng Sub-branch, Huihai Sub-branch, Puxieshi Sub-branch, Da'nan Sub-branch, Liming Sub-branch, Huajian Sub-branch, Laowu Sub-branch, Qinfen Sub-branch, Wutian Sub-branch, Quxi Sub-branch, Zhuangyuan Sub-branch, Shifulu Sub-branch, Cangnan Sub-branch, Hongchang Sub-branch, Chengdong Sub-branch, Shizhong Sub-branch, Railway Station Sub-branch, Dengfeng Sub-branch, Yinxin Sub-branch, Yongxing Sub-branch, Xincheng Sub-branch, CBD Sub-branch, Zhanqian Sub-branch, Xinqiao Sub-branch, Shuanglong Sub-branch, Chengnan Sub-branch, Shunjing Sub-branch, Qinye Sub-branch, Nanpu Sub-branch, Lizhong Sub-branch, Chengxi Sub-branch, Xueyuanlu Sub-branch, Shengcheng Sub-branch, Jiefanglu Sub-branch, Jiangbin Sub-branch, Baili Sub-branch, Jingshan Sub-branch, Development Zone Sub-branch, Haicheng Sub-branch, Binhai Sub-branch, Huanglong Sub-branch, Guoxi Sub-branch, Kunyang Sub-branch.

On December 14, 2007, upon the approval of File ZYJF [2007] No.298 by China Banking Regulatory Commission Zhejiang Regulatory Bureau, the Bank established Bank of Wenzhou Co., Ltd. Quzhou Branch on December 14, 2007.



##### (iii) Main business and service provided

As of December 31, 2007, the businesses of the Bank were the following approved by China's People's Bank and China Banking Regulatory Commission: accepting public deposits; issuing short-term, mid-term and long-term loans; handling domestic and foreign settlements; bill cashing and discounting; issuing financial bonds, entrusted to issue, cash and underwrite governmental bonds; buying and selling governmental bonds and financial bonds; inter-bank funds lending; foreign exchange trade and trade on behalf of others; operating bankcard business; providing L/C service and guarantee; authorized to collect and pay money or authorized to handle insurance services; providing safe deposit box service; other businesses approved by the banking regulatory authority of the State Council.

### II. Accounting Principle

##### (i) Statement on following Enterprise Accounting Principles

The financial statements and notes to the financial statements were released on January 31, 2008 upon the approval of the Board of the Bank.

The financial statements are complied with the requirements of Note II (ii) Basis for Preparation of Financial Statements below and truly and completely reflect the financial position, business outcome, changes in shareholders' equity and cash flow of the Bank.

##### (ii) Basis for preparation of financial statements

On the basis of constant business operation and according to the actually occurred transactions and events, the Bank follows the following principles to recognize and measure.

The Bank used to adopt Enterprise Accounting Principles and Financial Enterprise Accounting System. According to the Interim Rules on Recognition and Measurement of Financial Instruments (on Trial) published by the Ministry of Finance in 2005, the first date of executing the said rules is January 1, 2006. According to the Basic Enterprise Accounting Principles and other accounting principles (hereinafter the new principles or the new accounting principles) published by the Ministry of Finance in February 2006, the first date of executing the new accounting principles is January 1, 2007. According to the Interim Rules on Recognition and Measurement of Financial Instruments (tentative) and the new principles, the Bank made retroactive adjustments on the financial statements before the first execution date and prepare the financial statements of 2006 based on it. The transactions after January 1, 2007 were recognized and measured in line with the new principles and prepared financial statements on the basis of the new principles.

The fiscal year of the Company is from January 1 to December 31, on the Gregorian calendar.

##### (iii) Fiscal period

##### (iv) Currency for accounting

##### (v) Nature of accounting

The Company uses RMB as the currency for accounting

The Bank adopts accrual basis accounting system for accounting recognition, measurement and reporting. Except that tradable financial assets and available-for-sale financial assets are recorded at their fair value, the others are recorded at their historical costs. The fair value of the tradable financial assets and available-for-sale financial assets of the Bank means that in a fair transaction, the amount of asset exchange or debt payoff by

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="imgs/img_in_image_box_2333_214_2393_382.jpg" alt="Image" width="2%" /></div>


parties familiar with the situation and trade with their free wills. In a fair transaction, the two parties to the transaction should be enterprises in constant operation, not to or not need to go liquidation or reduce business size remarkably or trade under disadvantaged conditions.

##### (vi) Cash and cash equivalents

Cash refers to cash held by the Bank and deposits that can be paid at any time, including cash held by the Bank, non-restricted deposits for payment that placed in the central bank, funds placed in other banks that will be mature in three months, and funds lent to other banks. Cash equivalents are investment of short term, high liquidity, easy to convert to cash of known amount, and very low risk of value change, including bond investment maturity in three months and buying securities under agreements to resell.

##### (vii) Accounting for transactions in foreign currencies

Transactions in foreign currencies are accounted separately according to different currencies. At the end of the period, prepare financial statements in RMB. The principle for preparing financial statements in RMB is: prepare financial statements in each currency. Then convert the amounts in various currencies in USD. Then, convert USD to RMB and consolidate the statements to a financial statement in RMB.

Except for equity items, other items in the balance sheet are recorded in RMB by converting the foreign currency at the exchange rate at the end of the period. In the equity items, except for undistributed profit, other items are converted to RMB at historical exchange rate. The profit statement is converted to RMB at the exchange rate at the end of the period. The exchange rate adopted by the Bank is the benchmark exchange rate released by People's Bank of China and the cross rate accepted by the government. The differences from converting currencies for the items in the financial statements in various currencies enter into the gain or loss account of the period.

##### (viii) Financial assets and financial liabilities

## 1. Categorizing financial assets

According to the purpose of acquiring financial assets, the Bank classifies financial assets held to the following four categories: financial assets recorded at their fair value and the changes in fair value enter into the gain or loss account, including tradable financial assets and financial assets appointed to record at their fair value and of which the changes enter into the gain or loss of the period; held-to-maturity investment; loans and receivables; available-for-sale investments. Financial assets are recorded at their fair value upon the initial recognition. As to the financial assets which do not belong to the category of financial assets recorded at fair value and their changes entering into the gain or loss of the period, the related transaction expense directly attributable to the acquisition of the financial assets should be added in the initial recognition.

##### (1) Financial asset recorded at fair value with its changes entering gain or loss of the period

Financial assets at fair value and its changes through gain or loss of the period include financial assets held for trade or financial assets appointed by the management as the financial asset at fair value and its changes through gain or loss of the period at the initial recognition. Financial assets held for trade include financial assets bought for sale in a short period of time. Such financial assets are recorded at fair value afterwards. All realized or unrealized gain or loss enters into the gain or loss account of the period.

##### (2) Held-to-maturity investment

Held-to-maturity investment refers to non-derivative financial assets with fixed or certain recoverable amount and fixed mature date and the Bank has clear intention and ability to hold to maturity. Held-to-maturity investment is recorded at the amount of amortized cost calculated with actual interest rate method deducting the allowance for devaluation of the investment. The gain or loss on a held-to-maturity investment caused by being stopped recognition, devalued or amortization enters into the gain or loss account of the period.



If the Bank sells or re-categorizes high-amount held-to-maturity investment at the mature date (high amount refers to the total amount relative to the investment before sale or re-categorization), then the Bank should not categorize any such financial assets to the category of held-to-maturity investment. Sales or re-categorization meeting the following conditions are exceptional:

The selling date or re-categorizing date is near the mature date or redemption date (e.g., three months before maturity) of the investment so that the changes in the market interest rate have no significant influence on the fair value of the investment.

The sale or re-categorization happens after recovering almost all initial principal of the investment according to the agreed repayment mode or early repayment mode; or the sale or re-categorization falls into some indepen-dent event that the Bank is unable to control and predict reasonably and the event will not happen again.

##### (3) Loans and receivables

Loans and receivables are non-derivative financial assets that have fixed recoverable amount or certain recoverable amount and lack active market and the Bank does not have the intention to sell the asset immediately or in a short period of time.

The value of loans and receivables is recorded at the amount of amortized cost calculated with actual interest rate method deducting the allowance for devaluation of the investment.

##### (4) Available—for—sale financial assets

Available—for—sale financial assets refer to non-derivative financial assets of other financial assets that are not appointed as available for sale or investment not categorized to loans or receivables or held-to-maturity investment or financial assets at fair value of which the changes in fair value enter into the loss or gain account of the period. In subsequential accounting period, such financial assets are recorded at their fair value. The unrealized income caused by the changes in the fair value of an available—for—sale financial asset enters into capital reserve (other capital reserve) before the financial asset is stopped recognition or devalued. When the financial asset is stopped recognition or devalued, the accumulated changes in the fair value entered into capital reserve previously should be carried over to the gain or loss account of the period.

## 2. Loans of financial assets

##### (1) Categories of loans

Short-term, mid-term and long-term loans: The Bank categorizes its loans according to the due period of the loans. Loans that will be due in 1 year (incl.) are short-term loans; loans that will be due in 1 to 5 years (incl.) are mid-term loans; and loans that will be due over 5 years are long-term loans.

Import and export negotiation: refers to loan packages to customers in trade financing, negotiation under L/C, trade financing under export collection, commercial invoice financing and forfeiting under export T/T.

Discount refers to discounted payment to customers and other financial institutions that hold immature commercial bills.

Overdue loan: loan that cannot be paid back when it is due (including renewed term) because of the reasons of the borrower; or passive payment on behalf of others because the acceptor of the bill is unable to pay on time and the account balance of the discount applicant is insufficient; or passive payment on behalf of customers because the bill accepted by the Bank is mature but the account balance of the acceptance applicant is insufficient; or overdue import and export negotiation or off-balance-sheet payment on behalf of others such as L/C and guarantee, which is recognized as overdue loan from the day of paying the amount on behalf of others.

(2) Loans are recorded at the actual issued amount. Bill discount is recorded at the face value of the bill. The interest income of the discount occurring during the discount period is recognized according to the time and applicable interest rate of transfer the using right of the fund and enters into the gain or loss account of the related period. At the balance sheet date, the face value of the discounted bill and the unrealized interest income are

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="imgs/img_in_image_box_2333_215_2390_383.jpg" alt="Image" width="2%" /></div>


indicated in loan and deferred income of other liabilities of the balance sheet.

(3) According to Instructive Principles for Classifying Loan Risks [YF (2001) No.416] released by the People's Bank of China, the Bank classifies loans to five categories as normal, caution, inferior, doubtful, and loss. Normal loans refer to the loans that the borrower can perform the contract and the Bank has no sufficient reasons to suspect if the principal and interest of the loan can be fully paid back on time. Loan in the caution category refers to that the borrower has the ability to pay back the principal and interest of the loan but there are some negative factors that may affect the repayment of the loan. Inferior loan refers to that the borrower has obvious problem in solvency and the borrower cannot fully pay back the principal and interest of the loan depending on his normal business income. Even the loan is guaranteed, the Bank may have some loss on it. Doubtful loan refers to that the borrower is unable to pay back the principal and interest of the loan. Even the loan is guaranteed, the Bank will have a big loss on it. Loan in the loss category refers to after that all possible actions and necessary legal procedures, the Bank still cannot take back the principal and interest of the loan or just take back a very small part of the loan.

## 3. Financial liabilities

According to the purpose of financial liabilities, the Bank classifies the financial liabilities held to the following categories: financial liabilities recorded at fair value and of which the changes enter into the gain or loss account of the period, deposits, payables, bond payables and other financial liabilities.

(1) Financial liabilities recorded at fair value and of which the changes enter into the gain or loss account of the period

The Bank classifies financial liabilities recorded at fair value and of which the changes enter into the gain or loss account of the period to two categories: financial liabilities held for trade, and financial liabilities appointed by the management as financial liabilities recorded at fair value and of which the changes enter into the gain or loss account of the period upon initial recognition. All changes in the fair value enter into the gain or loss account of the period.

##### (2) Deposits, payables, bond payables and other financial liabilities

Except for bonds for trade or financial liabilities recorded at fair value and of which the changes enter into the gain or loss account of the period, other deposits, payables, bond payables and other financial liabilities are recorded at their amortized cost.

4. Stopping recognition of financial assets and financial liabilities

##### (1) Financial assets

When the contract for receiving the future cash flow of a financial asset expires, stop recognizing the financial asset.

##### (2) Financial liabilities

Only the present liability for a financial liability is lifted partly or entirely, can the recognition of the financial liability be stopped partly or entirely.

##### (ix)Subsequential accounting for real properties as investment

Real properties as investment refer to real properties held for gaining rental or capital appreciation, or for both purposes.

The real properties as investment of the Bank are recorded with cost method subsequently.

Real properties purchased or built by the Bank are recognized at their cost as the initial amount. To a real property transferred from a fixed asset, the initial amount of the real property is the book value of the transferring date.

<div style="text-align: center;">Years of depreciation and annual depreciation rate of real properties as investment are as follows:</div>

##### (x)Accounting for fixed assets

Fixed assets are tangible assets held for providing services, leasing or business management of which the useful life is over one year.

Fixed assets are recorded at the cost of acquisition. All direct or indirect costs related to the purchase or construction of the fixed assets arising before the fixed assets reach usable or salable status as planned, are capitalized to the cost of the fix assets. Depreciation on fixed assets is accounted on an average basis under straight-line method. The depreciation rate is determined according to the useful life of a fixed asset and deducting its residual value from the original value of the fixed asset. Expense of fixed asset renovation that meets the conditions for capitalization is depreciated separately with average useful life method in the shorter period of the interval of two renovations or the remaining useful life of the fixed asset.

<div style="text-align: center;">Main categories of fixed assets, years of depreciation and annual depreciation rate are as follows:</div>

##### (xi)Accounting for construction in progress

Construction in progress is recorded at its actual cost individually under each approved project.

When the construction in progress reaches the usable status as planned, carry it over to fixed asset. If the construction is not finished final accounting upon completion, carry it over at estimated value and adjust the value after the financial accounting upon completion is finished.

Intangible assets are recorded at their actual cost initially when it is acquired.

##### (xii) Accounting for intangible assets

The Bank analyzes and judges the useful life of an intangible asset in getting an intangible asset. If the intangible asset has limited useful life, then estimate the years of the useful life. If the beneficial period of the intangible asset cannot be estimated reasonably, the asset is recognized as intangible asset with uncertain useful life.

Intangible asset with limited useful life is amortized with straight-line method in its useful life. Intangible asset with uncertain useful life is not amortized.

Intangible assets with limited useful life of the Bank include land tenure and software.

##### (xiii) Accounting for long-term prepaid expense

Long-term prepaid expense refers to various expenses that have been paid but the beneficial period is over 1 year (excl.). Long-term prepaid expense is recorded at its actual amount and amortized evenly throughout the beneficial period, in which:

Prepaid rent for fixed assets rented under operating lease is amortized evenly throughout the years set in

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="imgs/img_in_image_box_2333_214_2393_384.jpg" alt="Image" width="2%" /></div>


the lease contract.

Expense on the improvement of fixed assets rented under operating lease is amortized evenly in the shorter period of the remaining lease term or the remaining useful life of the fixed assets.

##### (xiv) Accounting for assets for offsetting debts

Assets for offsetting debts are recorded at their fair value upon acquisition. Meanwhile, offset the book value of the asset being offset, including the principal of the loan, the recognized on-balance-sheet interest, other receivable, allowance for loss on loan or allowance for bad debt related to the loan or receivable. In disposing an asset for offsetting debt, if the income from the disposal is higher than the book value of the asset for offsetting debt, then enter the difference into non-operating income. If the income is lower than the book value, then enter the difference into non-operating expense.

##### (xv) Authorized business

The authorized business undertaken by the Bank is mainly released to authorized loans. Authorized loan release refers to the loan that the authorizes provides fund and the Bank releases, monitors, uses and helps collecting the loan on behalf of the authorizes according to the borrower, purpose, loan term and interest rate decided by the authorizes. All risks, gains or losses of the authorized business are on the authorizes' side. The Bank only charges a service fee.

##### (xvi) Accounting for purchase of assets under agreements to resell or sale of assets

##### under agreements to repurchase

According to the contract or the agreement, the Bank purchases an asset (including bonds or bills) from the other party of the transaction at a certain price. The Bank resells the same financial asset at the agreed price on the expiration date of the contract or the agreement. Purchase of assets under agreements to resell are recorded at the actually paid amount for the assets and indicated in "Purchase of assets under agreements to resell" in the balance sheet. To purchase of financial products under agreements to resell, the purchase of a financial product is deemed as a mortgaged financing transaction. The financial product purchased is the mortgage of the financing transaction.

According to the contract or the agreement, the Bank sells an asset (including bonds or bills) to the other party of the transaction at a certain price. The Bank repurchases the same financial asset at the agreed price on the expiration date of the contract or the agreement. Sales of assets under agreements to repurchase are recorded at the actually received amount from the assets and indicated in "Sale of assets under agreements to repurchase" in the balance sheet. To sale of a financial product waiting for repurchase, the financial product will be indicated continuously in the balance sheet of the Bank and accounted in line with related accounting policy.

The price difference of purchase of assets under agreements to resell or sale of assets under agreements to repurchase is recognized as interest income or expense at actual interest rate during the reselling or repurchasing period.

##### (xvii) Devaluation of main assets

## 1. Financial assets

At every balance sheet date, the Bank check the book value of the financial assets other than tradable financial assets in order to judge if there is any evidence showing the financial asset's devaluation caused by one or more events. The event causing devaluation refers to that occurring after the asset is recognized initially, and the event will affect the estimated future cash flow and the Bank can measure the influence reliably.

(1) Recording financial assets at amortized cost

If objective evidence proves a financial asset (including loan, receivable and held-to-maturity investment) recorded at amortized cost is devalued, then reduce the book value of the financial asset to the recoverable amount. The reduced amount is recognized as loss on the devaluation of the asset and enters into the gain or loss account of the period. The recoverable amount should be recognized as cash amount at the original actual interest rate according to the future cash flow (excluding the credit loss not yet happens) of the financial asset and taking into account of the value of related collaterals (deducting estimated disposal expense). The original actual interest rate is the actual interest rate upon recognizing the financial asset initially. Loans to businesses, receivables and held-to-maturity investments, if applied to flexible interest rates, the actual interest rate set in the contract may be adopted as the discount rate in calculating the recoverable amount.

The Bank assesses big-amount financial assets individually in order to determine if there is any objective evidence of devaluation. To financial assets of which the amount of an individual asset is minor, check the asset individually or combined together to determine if there is any objective evidence of devaluation. To a financial asset that has been assessed individually but no objective evidence of devaluation, whether the amount is high or low, the asset will be put into a group of other financial assets with similar credit risks for devaluation assessment again. To a financial asset that has been assessed individually and has recognized or kept recognizing devaluation, the asset will not be put into the asset combination group. If objective evidence proves the asset is devalued, then recognize loss on devaluation equaling to the difference between the present value of its future cash flow and its book value and provide for allowance for devaluation.

To the loans in the financial assets recorded at their amortized cost, the Bank adopts allowance method to account for the allowance for the loss on loan. The allowance for the loss on loan covers all loans the Bank bears the risks and losses. The allowance for the loss on loan includes specialized allowance and particular allowance. Specialized allowance is determined according to the risk degree and recoverable possibility of the loan asset. Particular allowance is the allowance provided for particular governmental loans.

At the end of the period, the Bank checks if there is any objective evidence of loss on the devaluation of the loan, in which, each big-amount loan is checked individually. Each non-big-amount loan is checked individually or together with other loans according to the actual situation. If no objective evidence of loan devaluation is found in checking loans individually, whether the amount of the loan is high or low, the Bank will put the loan into the group of other loans with similar credit risks to check and measure. If objective evidence proves an event that influences the future cash flow of the loan or the combination of such loans occurs, and the financial influence of the event can be measured reliably, then the Bank recognizes the loss on devaluation of the loan or the combination of such loans, and provides allowance for the loss on loan. The objective evidence of devaluation of loan includes but not limited to the overdue interest payment, principal repayment or fatal financial difficulties of the borrower.

If objective evidence proves that a loss on devaluation of a loan occurs, then the loss is recorded at the difference between the book value of the loan and the present value of the estimated future cash flow (excluding the credit loss not yet happens) calculated at the original actual interest rate. The loss goes into the profit statement. If the contracted interest rate of the loan is a flexible interest rate, then the discount rate in deciding the loss on devaluation of the loan is the present actual interest rate set in the contract. The present value of the future cash flow of a mortgaged loan is the result of the value of the pledge deducting the estimated cost of acquiring and selling the pledge.

If in the next financial reporting periods, the amount of the loss on devaluation decreases and the decrease is objectively related to certain events (e.g., the improvement of the credit rate of the borrower), then the Bank transfers back the amount of loss on devaluation recognized previously by adjusting the amount of allowance. The amount transferred back enters into the gain or loss account of the period. In writing off an occurred loss on loan after finishing necessary procedures, offsets the loss by the provided allowance for loss on loan. To loss on

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="imgs/img_in_image_box_2333_214_2393_383.jpg" alt="Image" width="2%" /></div>


Loan that is written off but collected afterwards, then the collected amount should enter into the gain or loss account of the collecting period and offset the allowance for loss on loan of the period.

##### (2) Available-for-sale financial assets

At the end of the period, if the fair value of an available-for-sale financial asset decreases and the decreasing trend is estimated not temporary by taking into various relative factors, then recognize loss on devaluation even if the financial asset is not stopped recognition. The accumulated loss caused by the decrease of the fair value that entered into capital reserve previously should be transferred to the gain or loss account of the period. The result of the difference between the initial acquisition cost (deducting the recovered principal and the amortized amount) of the asset and the present fair value deducting the loss on devaluation that entered into the gain or loss account previously is recognized as the accumulated loss of the transfer.

When loss on devaluation of an equity tool investment that is categorized as an available-for-sale financial asset is recognized, the loss should not be transferred back through gain or loss account. When the loss on devaluation of the liability tool of an available-for-sale financial asset is confirmed, the loss should not be transferred back.

##### (3) Financial assets recorded at their cost

To an equity financial tool without market price and is not recorded at its fair value because it cannot be measured with its fair value, if evidence shows that the equity financial tool is devalued, the amount of loss on devaluation should be the difference between the book value of the financial asset and the present value of the future cash flow of similar financial assets calculated according to the current market return rate.

If the recoverable amount of the asset is lower than its book value, then reduce the book value to the recoverable amount. The deducted amount is recognized as loss on the devaluation of the asset and enters into the gain or loss account of the period. Meanwhile, provide for corresponding allowance for devaluation of asset.

2. Long-term non-financial assets such as fixed assets, construction in progress and intangible asset

To long-term non-financial assets such as fixed assets, construction in progress and intangible asset, the Bank judges if there is any evidence of devaluation of the related asset. To intangible asset with uncertain useful life, whether or not there is evidence of devaluation, the Bank performs devaluation test on it every year.

If evidence shows an asset may be devalued, estimate the recoverable amount of the asset. The recoverable amount is recognized as higher of the result of the fair value of the asset deducting the disposal expense or the present value of the estimated future cash flow of the asset.

When the loss of devaluation of asset is recognized, the depreciation or amortization expense of the devalued asset is adjusted accordingly in future periods so that the adjusted book value (deducting the estimated net residual value) of the asset will be distributed evenly throughout the remaining useful life of the asset.

Once a loss on devaluation of asset is recognized, it should not be transferred back in the future accounting periods.

If the evidence shows an asset may be devalued, estimate the recoverable amount based on individual asset. If it is difficult to estimate the recoverable amount of an individual asset, determine the recoverable amount based on the asset group of which the asset belongs to.

The basis for recognizing an asset group is that if the main cash inflow generated by the asset group is independent from the cash inflow of other assets or asset groups. Meanwhile, in recognizing an asset group, the operating activity mode of the management of the Bank and the management's decision-making on the constant use of the asset or the disposal of the asset are also taken into account.

If a product (or other produce) produced by a combination of several assets has an active market, then even part or all these products (or other produces) are used internally, the combination of these assets is recognized as an asset group when the foregoing conditions are met. If the cash inflow of the asset group is affected by the internal transferring price, then determine the future cash flow of the asset group according to the best estimation of the future price in a fair transaction made by the management of the Bank.



Once an asset group is determined, it should be kept consistent in every accounting period.

## 3. Assets for offsetting debts

At the end of the period, the Bank checks if there is any objective evidence of loss on the devaluation of assets for offsetting debts. The allowance for devaluation of assets for offsetting debts is recorded at lower of the book value at the end of the period or the cash–realizable amount. Provide allowance for devaluation equaling to the difference between the book value and the cash–realizable amount. If the influencing factors on reducing the value of the asset in the book disappear, then recover the reduced amount and transfer it back from the allowance for devaluation of assets for offsetting debts that provided previously. The amount transferred back enters into the gain or loss account of the period.

##### (xviii) Interest income and expense

Interest income and expense are recognized in the profit statement pursuant to the accrual basis accounting principle with actual interest rate method. Actual interest rate method is a method to calculate the amortized cost of certain financial asset or liability and distribute the interest income and expense in the related periods. Actual interest rate is the interest rate used for discounting the future cash flow to the net book value of a financial tool on its mature date or in a certain proper short period of time. In estimating future cash flow, the Bank takes all contract terms of the financial tool into account, but does not take into account of future credit loss. In calculating the actual interest rate, the Bank takes into account of the transaction cost, discount or premium, and all expenses related to the actual interest rate paid or received by the parties to the contract.

##### (xix) Service charge and commission income

Service charge and commission income are usually recognized pursuant to the accrual basis accounting system in providing the related service. Commissions and service charges related to loan commitment are usually recognized throughout the commitment period with straight-line method.

##### (xx) Accounting for income tax

The Bank calculates income tax payable according to the applicable income tax rate, based on the total profit stated in the financial statement and by making adjustments on tax-exemptible income and undetectable expense pursuant to the applicable tax laws and regulations as well as their interpretations.

To the temporary difference of assets and liabilities caused by the difference of accounting and taxation basis, adopt debt method to recognize deferred income asset or liability based on the temporary difference. The temporary difference will generate taxable income in the future. Temporary difference refers to the difference between the book value and the taxation basis of the asset or liability. To account not being recognized as assets or liabilities, if its taxation basis can be recognized according to the tax law, then the difference between the book value and the taxation basis is also recognized as temporary difference.

The Bank checks the book value of the deferred income tax at each balance sheet date and when it is unlikely to have enough taxable income in the future to transfer back part or entire deferred income tax asset, deduct the amount of the deferred income tax asset that cannot be transferred back.

## (xxi) Changes in important accounting policies and accounting estimates during the reporting period and the influences of the changes

According to the Interim Rules on Recognition and Measurement of Financial Tools (on Trial) published by the Ministry of Finance in 2005, the stipulations in CK [2006] No.3 Notice of Printing and Distributing 38 Detailed Principles including Enterprise Accounting Principle No.1–Inventoreis published by the Ministry of Finance, and

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="imgs/img_in_image_box_2333_214_2390_382.jpg" alt="Image" width="2%" /></div>


Notice of Doing Well of Financial Accounting Information Disclosure Related to the New Accounting Principles (ZJF [2006] No.136) released by the Securities Regulatory Commission, and the stipulations in the Q&A No.7 of Regulations on Information Disclosure of Public Companies – Preparation and Disclosure of Comparison Financial Accounting Information in the Transitional Period of the Old and the New Accounting Principles (ZJHJZ [2007] No.10), the Bank decided January 1, 2006 as the first day of implementing the Interim Rules on Recognition and Measurement of Financial Tools (on Trial) and January 1, 2007 as the first date implementing the new accounting principles. The activities involved in the changes in accounting policies and accounting estimates as a result include:

1. The method of accounting for income tax is changed from tax payable method to debt method.

2. Measuring financial assets at their fair value.

3. Estimating the compensation and welfare for layoff employees

4. Recognizing interest income with actual interest method in line with the accrual basis accounting system.

#### III. Taxes

##### (i) Business tax

The taxes and tax rates applied to the Bank are as follows:

Business tax is 5% of the business revenue. The business tax of the sub-branches in the urban area of Wenzhou is summed up and paid by the Headquarters. Branches and sub-branches in counties (cities) pay the tax to their local tax administration. Business income includes loan interest income, income from intermediary services and income from other business; however, income from deals with financial institutions is not included.

City construction and maintenance tax is 5% or 7% of business tax. The business tax of the sub-branches in the urban area of Wenzhou is summed up and paid by the Headquarters. 2. Deposit reserve in RMB, deposit reserve in foreign currencies and fiscal deposit placed in the People's Bank of China are not allowed to use for daily business. The RMB deposit reserve ratio at December 31, 2007 and December 31, 2006 was 14.50% and 9% respectively. The foreign currency deposit reserve ratio at December 31, 2007 and December 31, 2006 was 5% and 4% respectively. The scope of RMB deposit reserve and foreign currency deposit reserve covers deposits of institutions, deposits other than fiscal revenue, deposits of individuals, deposits of corporations, credit balance of liabilities of authorized business offsetting assets, and other deposits.

3. At the end of 2007, cash and deposits in central bank increased 1,070,666,300 yuan compared with that at the end of 2006. The growth rate was 41.01%. The main reasons for the growth included:

(1) According to the regulation of the People's Bank of China on increasing the deposit reserve ratio, the RMB deposit reserve ratio of the Bank increased from 9% at the beginning of 2007 to 14.50% at the end of 2007. At the end of 2007, the statutory reserve placed in the central bank increased 863,878,500 yuan compared with that at the end of 2006. The growth rate was 70.28%.

(2)The business of the Bank has been growing yearly. To adapt to the constant business growth, the Bank increased cash in hand and excess reserve. At the end of 2007, cash in hand and excess reserve increased 191,388,800 yuan. The growth rate was 13.87%.

On November 28, 2006, according to the resolution of the 2nd shareholders' meeting of 2006, the Bank decided to issue RMB subordinated bond of 550,000,000 yuan through public offering on the inter-bank bond market. On July 6, 2007, upon the Approval of Subordinated bond Issuance of Wenzhou City Commercial Bank of China Banking Regulatory Commission (YJF [2007] No.278) and the Administrative Licensing

Letter of the People's Bank of China (YSCZYZ [2007] No.24 on August 27, 2007, the Bank was approved to issue commercial bank subordinated bond of 550,000,000 yuan through public offering on the inter-bank bond market. The financial bond was finished offering on September 14, 2007. The term of the bond is 10 years. The Bank has the right to choose if or not redeem all or part of the subordinated bond at the end of the fifth year. If the Bank chooses to exercise the right, then the term of the bond is 5 years. The bond is applied to fixed interest rates in different periods. The interest is paid once a year. The annual interest rate for the first five years is 5.50% of the face value. The value date is September 18, 2007. If the Bank does not choose to exercise the right, then the annual interest rate of the next five years is 8.50%. The bond is applied to simple interest method to calculate interest annually. Compound interest is not applied. No interest will be paid after the bond is mature. Interest is paid once a year. The payment of the principal and interest of the bond is after the deposits and other liabilities of the bank but before stock capital. The capital raised from the bond issuance would be used to supplement the supplementary capital of the Bank. The commission of the bond issuance was 3,575,000 yuan.

To personal saving account (excluding interest settlement) that does not have any receipt or payment in three years and the account balance is less than 5 yuan, the balance of the account is transferred to the long outstanding deposit account. If a joint-name card expires, the balance is transferred to the long outstanding deposit account.

#### The stock capital verification of the Bank is as follows:

May 22, 1998, upon the verification of Zhejiang Provincial Auditors' Firm and ZSYZ [1998] No.017 capital verification report prepared by Zhejiang Provincial Auditors' Firm, the stock capital of the Bank upon incorporation was RMB 290,495,800.00 yuan.

February 6, 2004, the Bank increased a capital of 180,300,000.00 yuan. The stock capital increased to RMB 470,795,800.00 yuan, which was verified by Wenzhou Huaming CPAs. Wenzhou Huaming CPAs prepared [2004] HYZ No.39 capital verification report to confirm the stock capital.

June 23, 2006, the Bank increased a capital of 536,417,731.00 yuan. The stock capital increased to RMB 1,007,213,531.00 yuan, which was verified by Wenzhou Huaming CPAs. Wenzhou Huaming CPAs prepared [2006] HYZ No.261 capital verification report to confirm the stock capital.

December 25, 2006, the Bank increased a capital of 15,968,390.00 yuan. The stock capital increased to RMB 1,023,181,921.00 yuan, which was verified by Wenzhou Huaming CPAs. Wenzhou Huaming CPAs prepared [2006] HYZ No.461 capital verification report to confirm the stock capital.

The main reason for the increase was the increase of loan increased loan interest income of 298,672,600 yuan, increasing 34.27%. Especially, the Bank focused on personal loan in 2007. The interest loan income from personal loans increased 228,738,300 yuan, accounting for 76.58% of the total loan growth.

Interest expense in 2007 increased 182,024,200 yuan compared with that in 2006 increasing 59.42%. The growth rate was 59.42%. The main reasons for the increase were:

(1) The increase of customers' deposits and People's Bank raised the interest rate for six times. Deposit interest expense in 2007 increased 90,080,900 yuan compared with that in 2006, increasing 39.31%.

L/C is a credit loan in which the Bank is requested and instructed by the applicant to issue a written guarantee letter of certain amount which guarantees to pay the amount in a given period at a given place upon given documents.

Bank acceptance bill is a credit loan business in which the payee or payer (or cashing applicant) issues a commercial acceptance bill, the cashing applicant applies to the Bank and the Bank agrees to cash the commercial acceptance bill after examination.

L/G is a credit loan business in which the Bank is requested by the applicant or authorized person to issue a letter of guarantee promising to the beneficiary that when the applicant fails to fulfill the liabilities and undertakings set in the contract, the Bank will cover the debt or bear the liabilities as ruled in the letter of guarantee.

## VIII. Events after the balance sheet date

On January 15, 2008, the 20th meeting of the 3rd Board of Directors of the Bank discussed and adopted resolution to initial public offering of A-shares. The meeting adopted the following resolution for the distribution of accumulated undistributed profit before the IPO: “If the IPO of A-shares is successful, then the undistributed profit before the IPO shall be shared by the old and new shareholders after the IPO.” The meeting also resolved that in distributing the profit of 2007, provide 10% of the audited profit of 2007 as statutory surplus reserve and 10% of the stock capital as dividend to shareholders. All remaining distributable profit is provided as general provision. In distributing the profit of 2007, if the amount of general provision does not reach 1% of the risk assets as of the end of 2007, then the general provision shall be provided fully before June 30, 2008. The above resolutions of the Board of Directors were discussed and adopted at the first extraordinary shareholders’ meeting of 2008 on January 31, 2008.

According to the above resolutions, as of December 31, 2007, after providing 10% of the profit as statutory surplus reserve, the accumulated undistributed profit was 295,506,590.88 yuan. Provide 10% of the stock capital, 102,318,192.10 yuan, as dividend to shareholders. After providing for the dividend to shareholders, the remaining undistributed profit was 193,188,398.78 yuan. As of December 31, 2007, 1% of the balance of the risk assets of

# 立信會計師事務所有限公司 Shu Lun Pan Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd.

All Shareholders of Bank of Wenzhou Co., Ltd.:

Internal Control Audit Report

XKSBZ (2008) No. 20570

We were entrusted to audit the notes to the effectiveness of the internal control related to the financial statements as of December 31, 2007 made by the management of Bank of Wenzhou Co., Ltd. (hereinafter the Bank). The management of the Bank is responsible for establishing and optimizing the internal control and keeping its effectiveness. We bear the responsibility to give our opinions on the audit of the effectiveness of the internal control of the Bank.

Our audit is based on Guideline for Internal Control Audit. During the audit, we learned, tested and assessed the properness of the design of the internal control and the effectiveness of implementation and carried out other procedures we deemed necessary. We believe our audit provided a reasonable basis for our opinions.

The internal control has intrinsic limitation and the possibility of false statement and undiscovered false information due to errors or fraudulent practices. Besides, the circumstance changes may cause internal control improper or lower the degree of internal control following the controlling policy and process. It has some risks to use the internal control result to speculate the effectiveness of the internal control in the future.

In our opinion, the criteria set by the Bank according to its Specifications on Assessment of Effectiveness of Internal Control kept effective internal control related to the financial statement in all material aspects as of December 31, 2007.

# Bank of Wenzhou Co., Ltd. Specifications on Assessment of Effectiveness of Internal Control

I. Internal Control Environment

##### (i) Governance Structure

Bank of Wenzhou Co., Ltd. (hereinafter the Bank) has established a corporate governance structure making up of Shareholders' Meeting, Board of Directors, Supervisory Board and the top management. Under the Board, the Strategic Development Committee makes the general business operation and development strategies for the Bank. The Risk Management Committee examines the standards on classifying the asset risks of the Bank, the policy for the provision and writing off of bad debts, the total amount of the provision for bad debts in a year, and review big-amount loan which exceeds 10% of the equity of the Bank. The Committee of Related Party Transaction Control is responsible for recognizing related parties of the Bank and reporting to the Board and the Supervisory Board, making risk management policies, and managing the application and termination of transac-tions with related parties. The Nomination and Compensation Committee studies the standards and procedures for choosing directors and members of the top management and gives advice, looks for qualified candidates for directors and members of the top management and gives advice, examines the job qualification and conditions of directors and members of the top management and gives advice, studies the standards and indicator system for assessing directors and members of the top management, assesses them and gives advice, researches and examines the compensation policy and plan for directors, supervisors, president and other high-rank managers and gives advice, and supervise the implementation of the plan. The Audit Committee organizes internal audit department to listen to the internal control assessment reports provided by the internal and external audit in situations and regulatory department and urges the top management to take corrective actions. The IT Management Committee has been set up and formulated IT development strategies. The Committee is responsible for the research and proof of the construction of major information systems, assessing the project result and giving advice. The Supervisory Committee gives opinions and advice on the internal control and risk management status of the entire bank. The Nomination Committee of the Supervisory Board examines the job qualification of the candidates for new supervisors and external supervisors. The Audit Committee hires independent agencies to conduct external audit on the annual business status of the Bank. The top management carries out various business activities under the authorization of the Board and reports to the Board and the Supervisory Board about the business development.

The Directors have setup independent Dependent director system, and the Supervisory Board has set up external supervisor system. By December 31, 2007, the Bank had had six independent directors (in which, the four new directors will be appointed officially after the bank regulatory authority approves of it) who had taken offices in various committees under the Board. In addition, the Bank has two external supervisors and three employee supervisors, being the chief and a member of the Audit Committee and the Nomination Committee respectively.

The Board, the Supervisory Board and the various committees under them formulated the rules on business discussion and process for decision-making and supervision. Each governance subject is able to exercise its responsibilities in line with its duties and rules and process.

According to the requirements on internal control of banks, the functional departments of the Bank fall into three categories as marketing department, risk control department, and operation and support department to separate front-end marketing, mid-end risk control and back-end support and assurance for various businesses.

#### (ii) Organization Structure

2. The position examining and approving credit is separated from account processing.

1. The position investigating credit and the position examining and approving credit are separated.

3. Centralized management of financial accounting.

##### (iii) Internal Control Policies

The Bank is able to formulate marketing policies, risk management policies and control and supervision policies that are complied with laws and regulations, the regulatory requirements, risk management and strategic development according to the economic policy, industrial policy and financial policy of China and the business strategies, market goals and development plan of the Bank. The Bank introduced in ISO9000 Quality Management System in 2006. It generally covers the internal control system for the management activities of various businesses of the Bank, falling into ten categories as corporate governance, credit approval (including general credit approval business, corporate business, and personal business), credit card business, international business, capital business, financial accounting and settlement, human resource, technology, internal audit, examination and assessment, and administration, support and others.

4. Centralized management of over-the-counter settlement business.

5. System development and system operation are separated.

### (iv) Company culture construction

The Bank is creating common values to instruct staff to deal with the relation between personal interest and collective interest and the relation between collective interest and social interest. The values will influence the development of the Bank, guide and regulate the behavior mode of the staff, and motivate their sense of responsibility and sense of master. Meanwhile, the Bank is developing fair, clean, law-abiding, service and diligent professional ethics of the staff, which regulate the behaviors between the Bank and society, the Bank and customers, the Bank and other banks, the Bank and the staff, and among staff members, encourage the staff to be enterprising, hardworking and disciplined, and urge all staff of the Bank to obey the law and do business in line with regulations. The Bank is making efforts to create good company spirit and company image.

#### (v) Human resource policy

The Bank is establishing a market-oriented HR management system, carrying out appointment and compensation system reform following the liberal market principle and optimizing staff incentive system. The Bank recruits and hires personnel, decides pay and assesses performance according to the positions, establishes incentive system and training system for different levels of staff so as to create a fair play environment for the staff.

## II. Risk Identification and Control

The Bank has formulated the rules, process and methods to identify, measure, monitor and manage risks and recognized and managed major risks such as credit risk, operating risk and ethic risk. The Bank is setting up related process and models to identify and measure market risk and liquidity risk. The top management is able to identify and control risks in time and sends the information to the decision makers via regular reports and irregular brief reports.

## III. Main Business Control Approaches

The departments of the Bank have formulated complete rules and regulations on daily business activities including credit approval business, capital business, intermediary business, foreign exchange business, and over-the-counter business. The process of each business has defined authorization and approval and can be reported to the financial accounting and related departments for recording, checking and filing the original vouchers.

##### (i) Control over credit approval business

The Bank has Risk Management Committee and Committee of Related Party Transaction Control under the Board and has established the decision-making system for credit management. The Bank separates loan examination and loan approval to enhance the credit risk control capability, optimizes customer assessment system and credit rating system, formulated Rules on Corporation Credit Rating Management and Rules on Management of Loan Quality Monitoring and Early Warning Reporting, and established credit approval, credit line management and risk monitoring management system. To the authority of credit and loan approval, each sub-branch is set authority limit and signed letter of re-authorization. Within the authority limit, the sub-branch has the right to approve loans and make payments. For loans out of the authority, the Credit and Loan Approval Department of the Headquarters will examine and approve the loan and the Fund Release Center will release the fund. The Bank has established credit approval business management and credit approval risk control over group customers and related-party customers, formulated Rules on Risk Management of Centralized Credit Approval for Group Customers and Implement Rules on Management of Transactions with Related Parties, set up post-loan management system and worked out post-loan examination process. The Bank has created and carried out the five-degree loan risk system, in which, normal and cautious loans are determined by the Risk Management Department after being examined by the sub-branch. The inferior loan is determined by the Risk Management Department. The loans of doubtful and loss categories are determined by the president of the Headquarters who supervises risk management. The Bank has established early risk warning system for credit approval business and formulated Rules on Management of Loan Quality Monitoring and Early Warning Reporting to reinforce risk control over credit approval business. The Bank has also set up the centralized non-performing assets collection and disposal system, established and carried out loan risky assets responsibility investigation rules to reinforce responsibility discipline and specify the responsibilities of the credit approval positions.



##### (ii) Control of Capital Business

The Bank has formulated Capital Business Control Process and carries out centralized management, different –leveled authorization and credit approval for capital business. The Bank has made capital business management rules and specified that the development and operation of new capital business should be approved by the authority of the top management. The Bank has worked out personnel and responsibility list and position descriptions to regulate the operation of capital operators. The Bank carries out capital operator authorization management to control the authority limit of the operators and the operating risks.

The operation, approval and accounting of capital business are separated. The front-end trade and back-end settlement are separated. The self-run business and brokerage business are separated.

The Bank gives necessary assessment on the risks and loss of capital business. Bond transactions are set stop-loss point. When the account of a single transaction loses 5% of the money, the operator must take action to stop loss. Borrowing and lending between other banks are set risk alarm line.

The Bank has laid down internal control rules on bond investment and determines the credit line and term of the trade partner and the investment object according to the credit approval principles and the financial position of the capital trade partner in order to enhance credit risk control. The Bank has made norms on capital business operation and checks it regularly. The Bank also formulated rules on business authorization management to account for capital business in a centralized way and check transaction diary and accounting books in time.

#### (iii) Control of intermediary business

The Bank has established normative Intermediary Business Control Process. In handling intermediary business, it is required to sign intermediary service agreement with customers and specify the rights and obligations of the two parties, business process, responsibilities of each party, capital transfer, commission payment and dispute settlement in the agreement. In handling payment and settlement business, it is required to check the bill or voucher according to the related rules in order to confirm the receipt and payment demand is correct and valid. Handle fund transfer procedures according to appointed mode, time and account. In handling foreign exchange business, the approval, operation and accounting bookkeeping are separated. Manage and check transactions strictly to ensure foreign exchange business conforming to the regulations. In authorized receipt and payment business, the Bank sets separate accounts for the transactions. The authorized receipt and payment are separated. It is required not to use or embezzle fund or pay on behalf of customers or involve in the disputes of customers. The Bank emphasizes the management of transmission and storage of important information.

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="imgs/img_in_image_box_2333_214_2393_383.jpg" alt="Image" width="2%" /></div>


such as important vouchers, bank cards, account passwords, stop-payment name list, and technical files to reduce the possibility of operating risks.

##### (iv) Control of over-the-counter business

The Bank has established Controlling Process for Deposit and Over-the-Counter Business and made related operating rules, covering saving, deposit, payment settlement and so on. The opening, change and cancellation of corporate and personal RMB checking account are pursuant to the Rules on RMB Checking account Management to check the authenticity, completeness and legality of the depositor's ID and account information. The Bank checks account opening, change and cancellation regularly to avoid depositors to rent or lend out accounts or use the accounts to do illegal activities. The Bank has established an account checking system to check the accounts between the Bank and customers, and the Bank and other banks. Internal account transfers and abnormal account changes are monitored. The Bank tracks and analyzes any unusual account changes. Over-the-counter transactions are implemented post-transaction supervision system. The operator and the supervisor are not crossed and their working places are separated. The Bank has established mistake reporting process and mistake correction and responsibility investigation system for major mistakes in overt-the-counter business.

## IV. Internal Control of Accounting System

(2) keep complete records of the details of business transactions in time;

The accounting system of the Bank follows the principles of authenticity, consistency and prudence and is able to do the following:

(1) record all valid business transactions;

(3) the value of business transactions are reflected in money correctly;

(4) business transactions are recorded and reflected in the correct accounting period; and

(5) financial statements and related notes can properly reflect the financial position, business outcomes and capital changes of the Bank.

## V. Control of Computer System

The Technology and Information Department of the Bank governs Development Division, Operation Division and Hardware Division, in charge of development and change, operation and maintenance management respectively. The "new-generation general business system" independently developed by the Bank covers transactions such as bank deposit, loan, bankcard, settlement, foreign exchange, internal account, online banking, intermediary business and ATM and provides management system data interfaces including financial management, credit and loan management, historical data center and performance assessment. It is designed to center on customers and comes with features such as broader accounting, RMB and foreign currency integration, automatic clearance and product management of bank business. In outsourcing management, the Bank has signed complete service agreements with external service providers to specify the rights, obligations and responsibilities of the two parties and set up contract, communication and information exchange mechanism. In addition, the Bank assesses and examines the business status, financial strength, credit history, security qualification, technical service ability and actual risk control and responsibility undertaking level of the outsourcing service providers every year. In managing the changes of versions, the Bank adopts cvs version control system to track and record the changes and updates of the information system. All systems are made plans before putting into use and designed "undo" and other technical features.



The Bank carries out risk analysis and business influence analysis, made backup strategy for the consistent business planning management, designed proper data, application and network disaster-tolerant plans for different disasters, and established a disaster recovery center in the same city.

## VI. Supervising and Correcting System

The Bank has formulated Internal Audit Controlling Process and established Internal Audit Department and Conformity Department. The Internal Audit Department gives objective and fair comments on the business management and the work performance of main responsible persons of the unit being audited and points out activities to be stopped and corrects activities breaking rules and regulations. To activities breaking rules and regulations seriously and personnel neglecting his duty at work seriously and causing loss, the Internal Audit Department would suggest to related department to investigate responsibilities. To problems found in audit, it may directly report to the decision makers of the Bank. To the problem found in business operation and account processing, it handles it in line with the Rules on Handling Breaking–Rule Activities and supervises the corrective actions. According to the conformity plan of the Bank, the Conformity Department instructs and urges each business line and branch to carry out conformity risk management to ensure the Bank run business legally and in line with regulations. The Conformity Department keeps daily work contact with the regulatory body, tracks and assesses the implementation of regulatory opinions and requirements, breaks down the regulatory rules, opinions and risk reminders issued by the regulatory department and gives opinions and advice to the management on effectively implementing these documents from the conformity view. The Conformity Department instructs staff on how to implement these documents, keeps tracing the implementation of these documents in the Bank, identifies and assesses the conformity risks related to the business activities of the Bank, including providing necessary conformity audit and test for the development of new products and new business, identifies and assesses conformity risks brought by the new business mode, new customer relation and major changes in the nature of customer relation. The Conformity Department is responsible for examining the legality and conformity of authorization and making letter of authorization, reviews risky loan responsibilities, and facilitates the Internal Audit Department in internal audit and internal control assessment.

## VII. Aspects to be improved in Internal Control and Corrective Actions

#### (i) Weakness in internal control

1. The Bank has established the corporate governance organizational structure consisting of the shareholders' meeting, the board of directors, the supervisory board and the top management and set up specialized committees. It is complied with the requirements on modern business management. But the Bank does not have Secretary of the Board.

2. To risk identification and assessment, the Bank has worked out a series of processes and methods for identifying, measuring and testing various risks and related management systems. However, these systems, processes and methods still have shortcomings in business coverage scope and model computation, especially, the ability of identifying, measuring, monitoring and controlling market risks need to be improved.

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="imgs/img_in_image_box_2334_214_2393_383.jpg" alt="Image" width="2%" /></div>


3. In credit and loan management, some sub-branches do not implement before-loan investigation system

and post-loan management strictly and the management of credit and loan information is not normative. Bill discount is under centralized credit approval management like loan business to quantify risks individually, but it has not been included in the credit and loan management control system.

4. The Bank has made great progress in IT construction. In 2007, the Bank was selected as one of the top 500 IT application enterprises in China. The Bank has set up technology information disaster backup system and carried out disaster recovery and business consistency plan drills. However, the Bank has not realized real-time data backup for different places. The ability to respond to natural disasters and the sudden changes in operation conditions need to be improved.

5. Because of tight staffing, staffing in some positions is unable to fully satisfy the requirements of internal control and business development. A number of important positions are unable to rotate regularly or implement compulsory leave.

6. The assessment system lays emphasis on business development. Internal control accounts for a relatively low proportion in the assessment system. The restrictive system needs to be enhanced.

7. The supervising and corrective system needs to be improved. A few internal control and corrective actions are delayed or incomplete.

##### (ii) Corrective actions

To the above weaknesses, the Bank has taken actions, made policies and process to improve the internal control system. At present, all corrective actions are under progress:

1. The Bank will further optimize corporate government structure according to the Articles of Incorporation of Bank of Wenzhou Go., Ltd. At present, the Bank is selecting a senior manager who is familiar with corporate government to be full-time secretary of the Board.

2. According to the requirements on business development and total risk management, the Bank is gradually optimizing the identifying and testing process, methods and measuring models for various risks to integrate qualitative and quantitative determination and try to cover all risks in the business process. The Risk Management Committee of the Board is quantifying the acceptable market risk level of the Bank to specify the stop-loss point. The management team is making risk management policy, process and detailed operating rules and allocating necessary manpower and material resources for market risk management in order to minimize the negative influence of market risks to the business activities of the Bank.

3. The Bank has updated and upgraded ISO 9000 Quality Management System and the Internal Control System and passed annual audit by an external institution, in which, a number of management documents relat-ing to credit and loan business have been amended completely. The credit and loan operation process is regul-ated further. In addition, the Bank has successfully developed an operating risk monitoring system, which has been put into use. The control over the operating risk of credit and loan business will be further reinforced. The Bank is optimizing the credit and loan management system to improve the management functions of the system. Bill discount operating process is to be included in computerized control. Meanwhile, bill discount and loan bus-iness will be combined under the centralized deposit and loan ratio management to reinforce control over liquidity risk.

4. The Bank will follow the requirements of the Guidance for Information System Risk Management of Banking and Financial Institutions to improve the security of the IT system and the emergency response to various accidents and vicious attacks. At present, catching the opportunity of cross-regional business operation in Zhejiang Province, the Bank is actively preparing for establishing information disaster backup center in other places of Zhejiang. Various preparations are under progress as planned.

5. According to the business expansion pace and the requirements of internal control, the Bank is optimizing staffing structure and recruiting professional managers and operators of different levels via all kinds of channels under the premise of unifying security, efficiency and effectiveness. The needs of over-the-counter business and credit and loan management will be put into priority. The internal control of important positions will be ensured.



6. Gradually optimize the assessment system. Under the principle of fully making use of the incentive system, raise the proportion of internal control management in the assessment system. By carrying out the Rules on Assessment on Internal Control of Branches of Bank of Wenzhou, assess and rate the effectiveness and completeness of various businesses of the branches objectively and thoroughly. The assessment results are quantified to performance indices, which link to the assessment on the branches and personnel so as to reinforce the internal control awareness, risk awareness and self-discipline awareness of staff in different levels and promote the internal control of the branches.

7. Further improve the supervising and corrective mechanism. 1. Reinforce the centralized management over the internal examination plan of the Bank. 2. Each business department and the Internal Audit Department reinforce the supervision over activities breaking rules and regulations, corrective actions and examination afterwards. 3. Activities breaking rules should be treated strictly under the Rules on Treatment of Activities Breaking Rules of Bank of Wenzhou.

In Conclusion, the Bank has set up proper and effective internal control system, which is complied with the reality of the Bank. The system plays an important role in regulating financial accounting behaviors, improving accounting information quality, enhancing business management, controlling operating risk, avoiding flaws and preventing malpractice. It guarantees the Bank's assets safe and integral, protects the rights and interests of interested parties related to the Bank, and improves the credit and market competitive strength of the Bank.
